title: Provision AWS Backup Plan
scenario: Your platform team needs AWS Backup Plan for a nightly backup schedule. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_backup_plan.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).
Tag the resource with Project, Environment and ManagedBy = "terraform".

focus.title: Complete the aws_backup_plan resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_backup_plan.

hints.why: `aws_backup_plan` is a real building block in production configurations. The exercise isolates one decision so you can recognise the same shape when it appears inside a larger module.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_backup_plan" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_backup_plan. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use this pattern when the requirement is part of a reusable configuration that another person or environment must be able to reproduce.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_backup_plan" "this"`. Use this code shape: name; tags; rule { rule_name; target_vault_name; schedule; schedule_expression }. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.plan_name`, `var.project_name`, `var.environment`, `aws_backup_vault.this.name`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
